profile.reading:
Csquare IAD1-C sits at 21110 Ridgetop Circle, Sterling, Virginia 20166, one of three buildings, IAD1-A, IAD1-B, and IAD1-C, on Csquare's IAD1 campus in Loudoun County's Northern Virginia data center corridor. Csquare, formerly branded Centersquare, was launched in April 2024 by Brookfield Infrastructure to combine Cyxtera, acquired out of Chapter 11 bankruptcy for $775 million in a deal completed January 2024, with Evoque, AT&T's divested data center business held by Brookfield since 2019. Csquare went public via IPO on NASDAQ in July 2026 at $21.00 per share. Csquare's SEC Form S-1 property table lists IAD1-C individually at 57,444 square feet sellable and 60.4 percent leased as of March 31, 2026, the largest of the three IAD1 buildings by that measure. Csquare's public spec sheet gives only a combined campus total across all three IAD1 buildings, 141,621 square feet of raised floor, 143.2 megawatts of utility power, 19.8 megawatts of UPS capacity, and 37.5 megawatts of generator capacity, with chilled-water cooling and SOC 1/2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, ISO 27001, and ENERGY STAR certifications applying campus-wide rather than broken out per building. All three IAD1 buildings are leased rather than Csquare-owned, per the SEC filing. Csquare does not name a power utility or year-opened date for IAD1-C. Dominion Energy serves Loudoun County as a matter of public record.

Csquare's Sterling, Virginia IAD1 campus sits within Loudoun County's Data Center Alley, the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world, alongside dozens of competing hyperscale and colocation operators within a few miles. Csquare's SEC S-1 discloses 389 megawatts of total sellable power capacity across its full 64-facility, 21-market portfolio as of March 31, 2026, and the same filing notes the company's legal predecessor entity, BIF III US Aggregator (Delaware) LLC, was formed in May 2018 as a Brookfield Infrastructure Fund III vehicle, well before the 2024 Cyxtera and Evoque combination that produced the assets tracked in this dataset. IAD1-C's Ridgetop Circle address sits roughly half a mile from IAD1-B's Nokes Boulevard address, both within the same fenced IAD1 campus, and this campus is a separate physical property from Csquare's IAD2 campus elsewhere in Sterling and its IAD4 campus in Ashburn, each of which carries its own address, its own building count, and its own campus-wide power and floor-space totals that should not be conflated with IAD1's.

sources.title: Csquare, Inc. Form S-1 Registration Statement

reading.body:
Centersquare's IAD1 campus in Sterling, Virginia comprises three buildings of which IAD1-C is the largest by leasable floor space at 57,444 square feet. The campus as a whole publishes 143.2 megawatts of utility power, 19.8 megawatts of UPS capacity, and 37.5 megawatts of generator capacity across all three buildings; the power and floor attributable to IAD1-C alone are not published. At a typical AI training density of 40 kilowatts per rack, the full campus utility capacity of 143.2 megawatts translates to roughly 3,580 racks, though this figure applies to the entire three-building campus and cannot be apportioned to this building without additional data.

The facility holds certifications for SOC 1 and 2 Type II compliance, PCI-DSS payment card security, NIST 800-53 PE High physical security, ISO 27001 information security, and ENERGY STAR efficiency. As of March 31, 2026, IAD1-C was 60.4 percent leased, the highest occupancy rate among the three IAD1 buildings. The campus sits on leased rather than owned land.

IAD1-C sits in Loudoun County's Data Center Alley, the world's largest concentration of data center capacity, alongside dozens of competitors within a few miles. Virginia has 330 mapped data center facilities across the state, of which 25 have published megawatt figures totaling 1,603.4 megawatts; the IAD1 campus ranks 26th by published capacity statewide. The utility serving Sterling is Dominion Energy, though the operator does not publish the year the facility opened or details of its grid interconnection.
